prerequisites: Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions (recommended)

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical-mathematical description of particle motion and know the magnitudes that quantify it.
Understand the laws and theorems that relate the motion of particles to the causes that provoke it.
Understand the concepts and principles necessary for the study of heat exchange processes in closed systems of ideal gases.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the subject.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Physical quantities. Treatment of measurement errors.
Thermometry and calorimetry. First law of thermodynamics.
teaching_methods: Presentation and defense of problems, assignments, projects
Use of simulation and/or experimental data processing software
Analysis of results and preparation of practical reports
Study of theoretical-practical contents presented in class and laboratory
Resolution of problems and preparation of practice reports, assignments, etc.
assessment_rules: The final grade NFO in the ordinary call is calculated as EvC + (1 – EvC/10) × CGO, where EvC is the continuous assessment grade and CGO is the global exam grade. A minimum of 3.5 out of 10 in the global exam (CGO) is required to combine with continuous assessment, otherwise NFO = CGO. A minimum global score of 2.0 out of 5.5 is required for continuous assessment to be considered, otherwise continuous assessment grade is zero. Any final score below 5.0 results in a FAIL. Extraordinary calls follow the same grading formula, with the validity of EvC extending to all extraordinary calls of the same academic year; a minimum of 3.5 in the extraordinary global exam (CGE) is required for combination.
